topics.title: Operator Overview
topics.summary: A compact map of the self-hosted Vocky surfaces.

blocks.text: The Admin UI is served from /admin and uses Admin REST only for protected dashboard, feedback review, and management data.

rows: Dashboard metrics plus feedback list, filter, detail, edit, and delete workflows

blocks.title: Auth boundary
blocks.text: Static Admin UI assets load without a bearer token. Protected Admin data stays behind /admin/api/*.

blocks.title: Browser edit scope
blocks.text: The Feedback view edits feedback_value, comment, channel, and tags. Captured user_id, trigger fields, target fields, messages, used context, source_metadata, and attributes stay read-only in the browser.

topics.title: REST Capture
topics.summary: Server-to-server feedback ingestion for trusted product and website backends.

blocks.text: Use POST /api/feedback from trusted server-side product code. REST uses the shared capture fields for website and product feedback, including user_id, trigger fields, page, widget, or product-surface feedback with target_type surface.

items.description: 202 Accepted with request_id, accepted_at, and status accepted.
Malformed JSON, schema errors, and semantic validation failures return 400 with a JSON detail field.
If capture cannot be queued, the endpoint returns 503 with detail capture queue unavailable.
When VOCKY_API_AUTH_TOKEN is set, /api/* requests must include Authorization: Bearer <VOCKY_API_AUTH_TOKEN>.
The channel field can be omitted, null, or one of web, mobile, and support. Blank channel input clears to null.
Send user_id when your backend has a stable product user ID. Send trigger_type, trigger_message, and trigger_metadata to describe the button, survey, rating, or manual workflow that caused capture.

blocks.text:
curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/feedback" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <VOCKY_API_AUTH_TOKEN>" \
  -d '{"message":"Pricing page feedback button was hard to find","source":{"product":"marketing-site","integration":"web-backend"},"comment":"I wanted to send feedback but did not notice the button","channel":"web","session_id":"sess_123","user_id":"user_123","trigger_type":"comment","trigger_message":"Pricing page feedback form","trigger_metadata":{"form_id":"pricing-feedback","placement":"footer"},"target_type":"surface","target_id":"pricing-page-feedback-button","target_text":"Feedback","tags":["website","pricing"],"source_metadata":{"path":"/pricing","referrer":"/"},"attributes":{"plan":"team","locale":"en-US"}}'

blocks.title: Capture only
blocks.text: REST capture does not expose public review, query, summary, job-status, or management endpoints.

blocks.title: Try creates feedback
blocks.text: The try form sends a real same-origin capture request. Use VOCKY_API_AUTH_TOKEN when /api/* auth is configured, and expect successful tries to create queued feedback records.

default_payload.message: 피드백을 보내주세요! prompt on the pricing page helped collect website feedback
default_payload.comment: The feedback call-to-action was visible and easy to use.

topics.title: Admin REST
topics.summary: Human/operator review and management endpoints under /admin/api.

blocks.text: Admin REST can inspect and manage all stored feedback records.

rows: Returns service, surface admin, and status ok
Returns dashboard totals and UTC daily buckets
Returns one record or 404 when missing
Updates review fields and returns the record
Deletes one record or returns 404 when missing

items: List filters cover the ingest-time window, source_product, source_integration, conversation_id, session_id, user_id, feedback_value, channel, target_type, trigger_type, tag, limit, and cursor.
Admin REST editable fields are feedback_value, comment, channel, tags, source_metadata, and attributes. Channel patch writes accept null, web, mobile, or support.

The Admin UI Feedback view supports list, user and trigger filters, detail inspection, editing feedback_value/comment/channel/tags, and guarded delete. Channel controls use Any/None plus web, mobile, and support.
The Admin UI target type filter uses Any, message, conversation, and surface. Any leaves older records with unset target_type visible; there is no dedicated unset target_type filter.
Filter by target_type message, conversation, or surface to review message, conversation, and product-surface feedback separately.
source_metadata and attributes are visible as read-only JSON in the Admin UI even though Admin REST can patch them.
user_id, trigger fields, target fields, messages, and used_context are captured context and remain immutable in this MVP.

items.description: Returned with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer when VOCKY_ADMIN_AUTH_TOKEN is configured and the request is missing or using the wrong bearer token.
Validation failures return 400, missing records return 404, and storage failures return 500 with JSON detail.

topics.title: Auth Tokens
topics.summary: Bearer-token variables for the two public-facing tracks.

blocks.text: Vocky is self-hosted for one deployment in the MVP. Bearer tokens are configured with environment variables and checked only on their matching HTTP path families.

rows: Set before exposing REST capture publicly
Set before exposing Admin REST publicly

blocks.title: Static UI access
blocks.text: /admin and /admin/assets/* are static UI routes. They do not require the Admin REST bearer token, but protected data requests to /admin/api/* do.

topics.title: Local Self-Hosting
topics.summary: Compose-first setup for a local or private Vocky operator.

blocks.text: Use the copied repo-root .env file as the shared configuration source for Docker Compose, Alembic, smoke checks, and pytest.

items.title: Create configuration
items.text: Copy .env.example to .env, then adjust host ports, publish hosts, or tokens before starting the stack.

items.title: Bootstrap
items.text: Run make bootstrap to sync host dependencies, start redis/postgres/app/worker, apply migrations, and wait for health.

items.title: Open Admin UI
items.text: Load /admin from the Vocky app. Static UI assets load without a token, while Dashboard and Feedback data use Admin REST.

items.title: Use an Admin token
items.text: If VOCKY_ADMIN_AUTH_TOKEN is set, paste that token into the Admin UI token field before checking protected /admin/api/* data.

items.title: Verify
items.text: Run make verify to inspect packaged Admin UI assets, wait for health, run the REST smoke flow, and execute the pytest suite.

items.title: Tear down
items.text: Run make compose-down when the local stack is no longer needed.

items.description: http://127.0.0.1:8000 when VOCKY_PORT is 8000 and VOCKY_PUBLISH_HOST stays on loopback.
VOCKY_BASE_URL controls host-side readiness and smoke checks.
make package-check builds a fresh wheel and verifies index.html, app.css, app.js, and docs.json are packaged for /admin.
TEST_DATABASE_URL must point at a separate disposable database from DATABASE_URL.

blocks.text:
cp .env.example .env
make bootstrap
open http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin
make verify
make compose-down

blocks.title: Direct-run fallback
blocks.text: If PostgreSQL and Redis are already running outside Compose, point DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL at them, then run uv run vocky and uv run vocky-worker in separate processes.

topics.title: Public Custom Domain
topics.summary: Generic HTTPS reverse-proxy setup for public self-hosted access.

blocks.text: Public deployments can expose Vocky through Cloudflare Tunnel, Caddy, or another HTTPS reverse proxy while keeping the Vocky process bound behind the proxy.

items.description: Use a generic public URL such as https://vocky.example.com and set VOCKY_EXTERNAL_BASE_URL to that origin.
Point the public HTTPS hostname at the local Vocky service, for example http://127.0.0.1:8000.
Run make external-verify after VOCKY_EXTERNAL_BASE_URL points at the live public origin. It waits for public health and then runs the REST smoke flow.

blocks.title: Expose only with tokens
blocks.text: Set both bearer-token variables before public exposure when REST capture and Admin REST are reachable from the internet.
